entry.evidence: produced a wealth of lithogeochemical data on the hydrothermally altered and mineralised host rocks (15,533 surface and drill-core assays)

steps.action: Frame the gap that PCA has not been applied to HS epithermal lithogeochemistry and ask whether PCA can track the geochemical evolution of Miwah and give exploration tools.
steps.quote: Miwah thus provides an excellent opportunity to use PCA to track the geochemical evolution of an HS epithermal system

steps.action: Take the company exploration assays (353 northern channel, 2,639 peripheral cliff, 12,741 drill-core samples) and split them into northern, peripheral and main zones.
steps.quote: All the lithogeochemical data used for PCA were supplied by East Asia Minerals (EAS).

steps.action: Build the processing chain: exclude elements with more than 30% below detection limit (with Mo and Sb exceptions), impute censored values by kNN, winsorize at 1.5 IQR, and clr-transform.
steps.quote: All censored data were imputed with the impKNNa (k-nearest neighbours algorithm) procedure

steps.action: Summarize assays by alteration type and zone with tables and box plots, then report Te, Sn and Bi correlations in auriferous silicified rocks.
steps.quote: the economically viable Au, Ag and Cu grades occur exclusively in the silicified rocks

steps.action: Run RQ-mode PCA (Grunsky script) on the clr data of each zone and read the metal associations of PC1 to PC7 from loadings, contributions and biplots.
steps.quote: Components PC1 and PC2, which cumulatively account for 70.2% (main), 66.6% (peripheral) and 62.6% (northern) of the total variation

steps.action: Repeat the PCA on the individual mineralised centres (Bluff, WBM, EBM) and along the periphery, and find PC variances within 1–3% of the zone-level PCA.
steps.quote: This narrow range of variances implies that the processes specified below operated similarly across the deposit.

steps.action: Run PCA separately on advanced and intermediate argillic wall rocks (northern zone surface samples and WBM drill holes) to see whether their metal assemblages mimic the main stage.
steps.quote: performed on individual advanced and intermediate argillic rocks

steps.action: Check the wall-rock PCA patterns in the same rock types from the Bluff and East Block M centres.
steps.quote: Similar patterns of metal assemblages are also observed in the same rock types from the Bluff and East Block M mineralised centres

steps.action: Map PC scores in 3D and in plan, and compare them with Au, Ag, Cu, Pb and Zn grade anomalies in each zone.
steps.quote: The plots show spatial relationships of negative PC1 scores with Au and associated metals and negative PC2 scores with Pb.

steps.action: Evaluate the PCA associations again with clr-clr bivariate diagrams (K, Ba, Au, Cu vs Al) using grade-scaled symbols, and identify K-poor 'outliers' and breaks in the Au trend.
steps.quote: clr-clr bivariate diagrams in order to identify indicators of geochemical processes

steps.action: Have whole-rock δ18O measured (BrF5 extraction, IRMS) on 3 peripheral and 2 Bluff-summit silicified samples.
steps.quote: Whole-rock oxygen isotope analyses of 3 samples from the peripheral zone and 2 samples from around the summit of the Bluff mineralised centre

steps.action: Compute fluid δ18O with the Zhang et al. (1989) quartz–water fractionation equation at temperatures taken from Mulja et al. (2020): 500 °C for periphery samples and 350 °C for summit samples.
steps.quote: we estimate that the isotopic compositions of the hydrothermal fluids in equilibrium with the peripheral samples are +6.18, +7.48 and +9.28‰

steps.action: Compare the fluid values with the Summitville whole-rock data and the magmatic-fluid range of Taylor and Sheppard (1986), and judge the peripheral fluids magmatic.
steps.quote: we interpret the estimated δ18Ofluid values from the peripheral zone to be predominantly magmatic

steps.action: Propose steam-heated oxidation, or limited interaction with connate waters, for the sulphide and arsenide oxidation.
steps.quote: the oxidation of the sulphide and arsenide at Miwah is attributable most plausibly to steam-heating oxidation

steps.action: Compare the PC1 loading order with the published volatility series of metals in volcanogenic epithermal and geothermal systems.
steps.quote: The above five metals constitute the most volatile elements found in volcanogenic epithermal and geothermal systems

steps.action: Interpret each PC as a past process: PC1 as magmatic gas condensation; PC4 as Cr-Ni-Co leached from Woyla serpentinite; PC2 as later Pb-Zn fluids; PC3, PC5 and PC7 as steam-heated oxidation forming scorodite and decoupling Au and Ag; barite precipitation for the K-poor outliers; cyclic sealing for the trend gaps.
steps.quote: the Miwah main-stage Au + Cu mineralisation in the main zone is also likely the product of the condensation of magmatic gases

steps.action: Reject three rivals: a different protolith for the outliers, a lack of data points as the cause of the trend gaps, and a distal porphyry Cu-Au reading of the northern-zone assemblage.
steps.quote: An alternative origin for the outliers from a different protolith is not viable

steps.action: Extend the Au versus Cr-Ni-Co separation as an exploration guide by citing Cr-rich vuggy silica at the Martabe HS deposit.
steps.quote: the host vuggy silica rocks at Martabe are also rich in Cr (up to 1,200 ppm; Sutopo, 2013)

steps.action: Keep the PCA-based evolution model (Fig. 16) and PCA as an exploration tool for HS deposits.
steps.quote: This study demonstrates the capability of PCA to identify the changes in the composition of the metal assemblages from the core through the periphery

tree.answer: Metal associations and alteration zoning in an intact HS epithermal deposit, read from PCA
No; the hydrothermal processes are past and are inferred from assay and isotope traces
Interpret alteration and mineralisation dynamics and derive exploration vectors
Few rivals, stated late: porphyry distal zone vs HS Au; different protolith; steam-heated vs connate waters
No distinct predictions derived for the rivals before comparison
Conditions found in traces of a past system, not set
PC variances stable across mineralised centres; wall-rock patterns repeat across centres; isotopes and mineralogy consistent
Process model kept as the most plausible explanation

end.claim: The PC1 Au-Cu-As-Ag assemblage records condensation of magmatic gases; PC2 records later Pb-Zn fluids; PC4 records a hybrid process in which Cr-Ni-Co were leached from serpentinite; PC3 and smaller PCs record later steam-heated oxidation; separating Au from Cr-Ni-Co by PCA is an exploration guide.

decisive_move.sentence: The zone-by-zone RQ-mode PCA of the clr-transformed assays produced the metal associations on which every process interpretation rests.

gates.evidence: The assays were collected earlier by the company for exploration; only five isotope samples were acquired, and these were chosen to determine the fluid source rather than to test a stated hypothesis (p. 5, p. 15). The process model was checked only for consistency, against literature volatility series, δ18O and mineralogy; no rival prediction was set up that could have failed. Processing parameters were the package-recommended values, and nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

novelty_claims.quote: To our knowledge, there has been no application of PCA to the lithogeochemical data of HS epithermal Au–Ag deposits
An important exception is the high-sulphidation (HS) epithermal class of deposits.

limits: Location limits: the supplied XML text contains only captions, so all body quotes and locations come from the PDF. No review file was supplied. The acknowledgements thank a named reviewer, an anonymous reviewer and the editor, and the dates show a year-long revision; what changed in revision cannot be coded. Data limits: the assays were produced by a third party (Intertek, for East Asia Minerals); QA/QC rests on a cited re-analysis (Taylor 2011). The isotope argument uses only five samples, analysed with weathered material partly retained, at temperatures assumed from the authors' earlier paper. Coding judgments (inference): no rival was given distinct predictions, and the process attribution of each PC is argued by analogy and literature, so the headline status is best_explanation. A sub-claim, PCA as a rapid exploration tool for HS deposits, is capability_characterized at best; it is not tested on a held-out or independent deposit, and the Sumatra-wide extension rests on a cited Cr datum from Martabe. Inconsistencies in the text (inference): loadings orders are cited as 'Table 2b' where Table 3b holds the loadings, and Fig. 13 refers to outliers 'from Fig. 11'. These are cross-referencing errors, not changes of method. The subset checks (mineralised centres) are coded robustness, not replication, because they reuse the same dataset.

disagreements.target: Published HS epithermal studies that use lithogeochemical data only for grades, zoning and mass balance
disagreements.support: The paper applies multivariate PCA to a large HS dataset and argues that it reveals processes and exploration vectors that these uses miss.
disagreements.quote: similar data for high-sulphidation (HS) epithermal Au–Ag ± Cu systems in the published, peer-reviewed literature are mostly treated as peripheral

disagreements.target: Mulja et al. (2020), vapour expansion model of Henley and Berger (2011) at Miwah
disagreements.support: It recasts the mechanism as condensation of magmatic gas mixtures recorded in PC1, supported by the volatility order of the PC1 loadings and by δ18O.
disagreements.quote: Although Mulja et al. (2020) invoked the vapour expansion model of Henley and Berger (2011) as the mineralisation mechanism at Miwah

disagreements.target: Mulja et al. (2020), analysis restricted to samples grading > 0.2 ppm Au
disagreements.support: It extends the analysis to all variably altered host rocks in three zones.
disagreements.quote: presented the mineralisation and lithogeochemistry of the deposit to samples grading > 0.2 ppm Au

disagreements.target: Chen et al. (2019), excluding PCs dominated by elements from unfavourable rock types
disagreements.support: It argues that the Cr-Ni-Co PC should be kept as an exploration guide, because the hyperacid-fluid interpretation links it to HS mineralisation.
disagreements.quote: the PC with a substantial variability of these elements could be excluded in subsequent analyses

alternatives_considered.chosen: Exclude elements with more than 30% of values below detection limit, but keep Mo (main zone) and Sb (main and peripheral zones)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Strict application of the 30% threshold (would drop Mo and Sb)
alternatives_considered.reason: Threshold recommended by Martin-Fernandez et al. (2012); Mo low values come from barren argillic rocks; Sb is closely associated with Cu and anomalous in silicified rocks

alternatives_considered.chosen: kNN imputation with k = 6 (k = 3 and 5 for small subsets), Aitchison metric
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Other k values for small subset populations

alternatives_considered.reason: Outliers can create a masking effect that distorts the PCA model
Avoids closure effects; clr data are less subjective and less abstract and suit biplots

alternatives_considered.chosen: Al as the reference for alteration intensity in bivariate plots
alternatives_considered.reason: Insufficient Si data for statistical analysis

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Limited interactions with locally derived connate waters
alternatives_considered.reason: Slightly enriched δ18O of summit samples, restricted oxidation along fractures, and lack of a supergene blanket

alternatives_considered.chosen: Barite-forming reaction for the K-poor high-grade outliers
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Origin of the outliers from a different protolith
alternatives_considered.reason: Precursors most likely came from a common magma reservoir (Mulja et al., 2020)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Cyclic decompression and silica sealing for the gaps in the silicification trend
alternatives_considered.reason: 7,736 drill-core and 1,888 channel assays of vuggy-massive silica

alternatives_considered.chosen: Northern-zone assemblage related to HS Au mineralisation
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Distal zone of porphyry Cu + Au mineralisation
alternatives_considered.reason: High actual contributions of Au to PC3 (39%) and PC5 (22%)
